meta.subject: Meghan Clarisse Cave — IG/FB algorithm playbook

instagram.notes: The profile URL https://www.instagram.com/meghanclarissecave/ (and the ?hl=en variant) returned an empty/blocked response on direct fetch — Instagram serves a login wall or JS-rendered shell to non-authenticated fetchers, so no bio, follower count, or post grid could be read directly. Search-indexed snippets confirm the handle @meghanclarissecave exists, is tagged by other local accounts (e.g. a November 2024 post from @cafeole_ promoting a performance), and at least one Reel permalink (instagram.com/reel/DXSmDm-kQhu/) is indexed, confirming she posts Reels. No numeric follower count, bio text, or post-mix ratio is exposed in any indexed search snippet.

facebook.notes: The exact URL https://www.facebook.com/meghancave/ returned an empty/blocked response on direct fetch (Facebook requires login for profile/page content). Search indexing points to what is very likely the same artist's actual Facebook Page under a different vanity name: facebook.com/meghanclarisse ('Meghan Clarisse Music'), category Americana/Rock/Country, reported via search snippet at roughly 1.2K followers / ~200 following, promoting the 'Kindred Spirits' EP and a poetry book. This could not be confirmed as the identical entity behind the /meghancave/ URL given in the brief (it may redirect, be a legacy/duplicate handle, or a distinct secondary page) — treat the 1.2K figure as medium-confidence and unverified against the exact requested URL.

profileScan.scanLimitations: Both Instagram and Facebook block unauthenticated programmatic fetches of profile pages (return empty bodies / require login), consistent with Meta's standard anti-scraping behavior — this is expected and was not bypassed, per instructions not to log in. All profile-adjacent facts in this file come from: (1) the artist's own website megcmusic.com (fetched directly, high confidence), (2) third-party press coverage (CanvasRebel, Shoutout Colorado, Bold Journey, FoCoMA, local venue listings), and (3) search-engine-indexed snippets/metadata of the IG and FB pages, which do not include real-time follower counts, full bios, or post grids. No follower counts could be confirmed with high confidence for either platform. Numbers above are marked null in structured fields precisely because they could not be verified against the exact URLs given; the FB 1.2K figure is preserved only as narrative context in 'notes', not as a verified data point.

rules.title: Shares (DM sends) outrank likes by a wide margin — build for the send, not the like
rules.rule: Design Reels around a moment a fan would forward to one specific friend (e.g., tagging a friend with 'we need to go to this' or 'this is so us'), not around maximizing likes. Treat the caption's job as prompting a send, and check 'sends per reach' in Insights as a primary health metric alongside watch time.
rules.evidence: Adam Mosseri has repeatedly named watch time, sends per reach, and likes per reach as the top cross-surface ranking signals (confirmed via his own Reels/posts, e.g. instagram.com/p/DFFyRp-pINJ, referenced by Hootsuite). Multiple 2026 industry analyses (Later, Hootsuite, Hypebot citing an April 2026 Podswap reverse-engineering study of 2,500+ niches) converge on shares/DM-sends being weighted several times higher than likes for distribution beyond the initial audience, with one estimate of roughly 4x weighting and a 'share-to-DM velocity' signal.

rules.title: Saves are the second-strongest signal — give fans a reason to bookmark, not just watch
rules.rule: Publish some content with clear 'utility' a fan would save to revisit — set-list previews, a chord/lyric snippet, 'venues I love playing in Colorado,' behind-the-scenes gear or songwriting notes. Don't make every post pure performance footage; mix in save-worthy carousels alongside Reels.
rules.evidence: Multiple 2026 sources report saves were elevated to a top-tier ranking signal in a 2026 update (one source cites a February 2026 Instagram Creator Education post ranking saves above comments and near watch time). Carousels in particular are documented to earn 3-4x the save rate of a comparable Reel from educational/utility accounts, per Socialinsider-style benchmark analysis.

rules.title: Small accounts are not disadvantaged — a strong Reel from a small profile can match a big account's reach, but it must clear sequential 'trial' gates
rules.rule: Post consistently (aim for 3-5 Reels/week — Instagram needs enough volume to run its tests) and treat every Reel's first hour as a gate: if it doesn't get strong early watch-time/save/share signal from your existing (small) audience, it won't advance to the non-follower test pool. Use Trial Reels deliberately to test hooks/formats against cold (non-follower) audiences before deciding whether to promote a video further.
rules.evidence: Instagram's own Trial Reels feature (help.instagram.com/1013292530224018) is designed explicitly to show a Reel to non-followers first and gauge performance before wider distribution — confirmed by Instagram's Help Center and demonstrated by Mosseri himself. Industry write-ups describe this as a staged/gated funnel: an initial small-audience test, then a widening non-follower test, with signal ratios (watch time, shares, saves, profile clicks vs. impressions) gating advancement. Multiple sources agree follower count under ~50K is 'the sweet spot' where engagement quality, not audience size, determines reach.

rules.title: TikTok watermarks and recycled/reposted content are actively suppressed
rules.rule: Never cross-post a Reel that still carries a TikTok (or CapCut) watermark/logo — re-export clean, native-resolution vertical video for Instagram. Avoid re-uploading the identical Reel repeatedly; Instagram's originality detection can exclude accounts with heavy repost patterns from recommendations entirely.
rules.evidence: Instagram's own creator guidance (Mosseri's posted 'Reels basics' video, referenced across Hootsuite/Later) explicitly lists 'non-watermarked, original content' as a baseline requirement for recommendation eligibility. Multiple 2026 sources describe an 'Originality Score' and cite accounts with 10+ reposts in 30 days being excluded from recommendations; watermarked reposts are described as actively detected and suppressed.

rules.title: External links in captions quietly cut reach; keep links out of captions and use bio / Stories link sticker instead
rules.rule: Never put megcmusic.com or ticket/merch links directly in a Reel or feed caption. Route traffic via the bio link or a Stories link sticker instead. The literal phrase 'link in bio' does not hurt reach — it's the actual clickable URL in the caption that does.
rules.evidence: Multiple 2026 analyses estimate reach penalties from in-caption external links ranging from ~19% lower median reach up to 40-60% reduction versus an otherwise identical linkless post, attributed to Instagram's preference for keeping users in-app. Separately, Mosseri has explicitly debunked the idea that saying 'link in bio' (the phrase itself) hurts reach — the penalty is tied to the presence of an actual outbound URL, not the words used to reference it.

rules.title: Engagement bait (comment-to-unlock, tag-3-friends, follow-for-follow) caps a post at its seed audience and can drag account-level trust
rules.rule: Avoid transactional prompts like 'comment YES for the link' or 'tag 3 friends who need this' — use open-ended questions instead (which still perform fine). Reserve CTAs for genuine calls to action (e.g., 'which song should I play at the show Friday?') rather than manipulative engagement loops.
rules.evidence: Meta's own Transparency Center has a dedicated Engagement Bait policy page defining and penalizing this pattern (confirmed primary source, though the fetched page returned only metadata with the core content behind further navigation). Independent 2026 analyses describe the mechanism as post-level demotion (the post stays capped in its seed audience) with a slower account-level 'drag' effect from a pattern of bait captions — corroborated by two independent industry write-ups.

rules.title: Raw, human-shot content is outperforming polished/AI-flavored production, and Instagram is explicitly deprioritizing low-authenticity AI content in 2026
rules.rule: Favor phone-shot, imperfect rehearsal clips, backstage moments, and human-voiced intros over highly produced music-video-style edits. Lead Reels with a spoken hook or visible human perspective in the first 1.5-3 seconds rather than a polished montage; use Trial Reels to test which raw clips earn distribution before committing studio-quality edits.
rules.evidence: Adam Mosseri's December 31, 2025 year-end memo (posted natively on Instagram, covered by multiple outlets) explicitly stated Instagram would prioritize 'raw, real human content' over AI-generated/overly polished material through 2026. This is corroborated by the April 2026 Podswap study (via Hypebot) finding raw phone-shot visuals outperforming studio-produced content by roughly 35% in discovery feeds, and by Mosseri's own posted guidance on hooks in the first 1.5-3 seconds.

rules.title: Facebook Reels are the fastest current growth lever, and Facebook is actively boosting same-day creator Reels
rules.rule: Post Reels natively to Facebook (not just as an afterthought cross-post) and keep them under ~90 seconds. Treat Facebook Reels as a distinct growth channel worth dedicated posting, not just a mirror of Instagram.
rules.evidence: Facebook's Head of Feed, Tom Alison, is on record (Oct 2025) stating the Reels algorithm was updated to surface '50% more reels from creators published that day,' and has publicly encouraged creators to increase posting rate ('posting more can help you break through'). Corroborated by two independent 2026 industry analyses (SocialBee, Postoria) describing Reels/short-form video as the fastest current growth path on Facebook.

rules.title: Facebook Events are still the strongest native tool for live-show promotion, and RSVP activity compounds through social proof
rules.rule: Create a public Facebook Event for every show, tag the venue and any co-billed artists, and post show-specific, city-named updates in the week before ('Can't wait to play [City] on Friday'). Ask co-billed artists to cross-promote — a 3-artist bill that cross-promotes can triple each artist's individual reach.
rules.evidence: Two independent musician-marketing sources (Chartlex, Eventbrite/Yapsody-style guides) converge on Facebook Events as the standout native format for show promotion, citing the RSVP-to-network-visibility mechanic as a compounding, algorithm-friendly signal, plus explicit local-area Events-tab discovery surfacing.

rules.title: Meaningful Social Interactions still govern Feed — genuine comments/shares/conversation outrank passive likes, and engagement bait is losing value
rules.rule: Write captions that invite a real reply or debate (e.g., asking fans to vote on a setlist song, share a memory tied to a lyric) rather than generic 'Are you excited?' prompts. Reply to comments to keep the conversation compounding — this is a ranking signal, not just courtesy.
rules.evidence: Corroborated by two independent 2026 Facebook-algorithm breakdowns describing Meta's continued 'Meaningful Social Interactions' emphasis: posts sparking back-and-forth discussion and shares are favored, while low-effort/bait interactions contribute less to reach than in past years.

rules.title: Watermarked/recycled cross-posts are suppressed on Facebook exactly as on Instagram, but same-video cross-posting without a watermark is not penalized
rules.rule: It's fine to post the same clean, non-watermarked Reel to both Instagram and Facebook — there's no cross-platform duplicate-content penalty for that. But never let a TikTok/CapCut watermark reach Facebook; re-export clean video for each platform.
rules.evidence: Industry sources agree platforms cannot detect duplicate content across separate services (so same-video, watermark-free cross-posting between IG and FB is not penalized), but that visible third-party watermarks (TikTok, CapCut) are actively detected and suppressed by Meta's ranking systems on both surfaces — a distinction confirmed by two independent write-ups.

rules.title: Facebook's audience skews older and is a stronger fit for country/Americana's core demographic and local-market reach than Instagram
rules.rule: Treat Facebook as the primary channel for reaching the 35+, Front Range/Colorado local audience most likely to buy tickets and attend shows — post local, venue-tagged updates and lean on Events; treat Instagram as the discovery/growth channel for younger and out-of-market fans.
rules.evidence: Two independent 2026 demographic analyses (Sprout Social, Hootsuite) confirm Facebook's user base has shifted meaningfully older (every cohort above 35 growing share, every cohort below 25 declining, with 65+ users disproportionately choosing Facebook), while Instagram Reels interactions skew 18-34. A musician-marketing source (Dynamoi) explicitly frames Facebook as better suited to country/classic-rock acts with a 35+ core audience and better cost-per-RSVP for regional/local touring acts.

rules.title: Facebook Reels distribution to non-followers is comparatively weaker than Instagram's — Facebook rewards existing-network conversion more than cold discovery
rules.rule: Don't expect a Facebook Reel to break out to strangers the way an Instagram Reel can. Use Facebook primarily to deepen engagement with people who already know Meghan (past show attendees, email list, local scene) rather than as a cold-audience discovery engine; save discovery-oriented experimentation for Instagram.
rules.evidence: One direct industry synthesis states Meta surfaces Reels to non-followers 'far more aggressively' on Instagram than on Facebook, framing Instagram as stronger for cold-audience discovery and Facebook as stronger at converting existing networks. This is a single clearly-stated source; treat as medium-to-low confidence pending a second corroborating primary-source citation, though it is consistent with the broader finding (fb-05) about Facebook's relationship-driven ranking model.

divergences.instagram: Instagram's Explore/Reels systems actively push content to non-followers via a staged trial funnel (Trial Reels, sequential test windows), making it the stronger channel for reaching people who have never heard of Meghan — especially younger, out-of-market fans.
divergences.facebook: Facebook's ranking model leans more heavily on existing relationships and Meaningful Social Interactions; Reels get a same-day creator boost but non-follower discovery is reported as comparatively weaker than Instagram's.
divergences.recommendation: Use Instagram as the primary discovery/growth engine (new fans, younger audience, cold reach) and Facebook as the primary conversion/retention engine (show RSVPs, ticket sales, deepening relationships with the existing Front Range fanbase and 35+ core demographic).

divergences.instagram: Skews younger (Reels interactions concentrated in 18-34), better for reaching new/out-of-market listeners and building a national/touring fanbase over time.
divergences.facebook: Skews notably older (growing share above 35, especially 65+), a strong demographic match for country/Americana and for the local Colorado ticket-buying audience.
divergences.recommendation: Don't treat the two platforms as the same audience with two upload buttons. Consider genre-appropriate content splits: Facebook can carry more local-show-specific, direct 'buy tickets/RSVP' messaging aimed at an older, already-warm audience; Instagram should lean more on discovery-oriented, shareable 'bridge' content aimed at growing the base.

divergences.topic: Native Reels vs. cross-posted Reels performance
divergences.instagram: No independent-source data was found directly quantifying native-IG-Reel vs. cross-posted-from-elsewhere performance differences on Instagram itself beyond the general originality/repost penalty (ig-04, ig-07) — the penalty is about detectable staleness/watermarks, not the act of cross-posting per se.
divergences.facebook: One source states Facebook's algorithm gives 'user-generated'/original Reels roughly 3.2x more organic reach than content repurposed from other platforms, and separately confirms same-video, watermark-free cross-posting between IG and FB itself carries no penalty.
divergences.recommendation: The clearest, best-supported version of 'native beats cross-posted' is about removing third-party watermarks and avoiding stale/recycled reposts — not about whether the same clean video is shared to both IG and FB. Post the same clean Reel natively to both apps (not routed through a TikTok-style badge or auto-poster that leaves a watermark), and treat the underlying originality of the footage, not the platform-to-platform sharing itself, as the primary reach factor. This finding is graded medium confidence — the 3.2x figure comes from a single source (autofaceless.ai) and was not independently corroborated with a second source; treat the ratio itself as directional, not precise.

divergences.instagram: External links in captions face a measurable reach penalty (est. 19-60% reduction depending on source); links belong in bio or Stories stickers.
divergences.facebook: No comparable link-penalty pattern was found in Facebook-specific 2026 sources; Facebook Events (which function as a structured, algorithm-favored 'link') and direct ticket/venue links in posts are treated as normal, expected content, especially for show promotion.
divergences.recommendation: Be link-shy on Instagram (bio/Stories only); be comfortable posting direct ticket links, venue links, and Event links in Facebook posts and Event descriptions, since Facebook's local-event discovery mechanics are built around exactly this kind of structured, linked content.

postingWindows.instagram: General 2026 benchmark data (Buffer, aggregated across niches) points to weekday mid-mornings (9-11am) and lunch (12-1pm) as strong Feed windows, with weekday evenings (7-9pm in the ET-based studies, i.e. roughly 5-7pm Mountain) as the best window specifically for Reels; one music/arts-specific note states music and arts accounts see strong performance late in the evening for new-release/BTS content. A separate reverse-engineered 2026 study found Monday the best-performing day overall and Tuesday the worst. Practical Mountain-time recommendation for Meghan: post Reels on weekday evenings roughly 5-7pm MT (aligning with the 7-9pm ET data point converted to Mountain), test Monday as a lead posting day, and use Instagram's own audience-specific 'Best Time to Post' insight in the Professional Dashboard to fine-tune once enough native data exists — general benchmarks are a starting point, not a substitute for account-level data.
postingWindows.facebook: No Facebook-specific, timezone-granular 'best time to post' dataset was found with strong sourcing in this research pass; general social-media benchmark guides bundle Facebook into cross-platform 'weekday 9am-1pm and 7-9pm' windows without Facebook-specific music-audience data. Given Facebook's older, local, event-driven audience for Meghan, the most defensible approach (medium/low confidence, inferred rather than directly sourced) is to post show-specific and Event-linked content in early-to-mid evening Mountain time (roughly 6-8pm MT) on weekdays, when an older local audience is likely browsing after work, and to post Event updates 2 weeks out and again in the final week before a show, per the two-touch cadence recommended in musician-specific FB Events guides.
